contract: get_observation(state) -> 1-D float array (length 1..512) and compute_reward(state, action, next_state) -> scalar float, both JAX-traceable (jit and vmap) functions of an XLand-MiniGrid 0.9.3 state: state.grid (H, W, 2) uint8 [tile id, colour id] indexed [row, col] (tiles: 0 empty, 1 floor, 2 wall, 3 ball, 4 square, 5 pyramid, 6 goal, 7 key, 8 locked door, 9 closed door, 10 open door, 11 hex, 12 star; colours: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 purple, 5 yellow, 6 grey, 7 black (floor), 8 orange, 9 white, 10 brown, 11 pink), state.agent.position (2,) uint8 [row, col], state.agent.direction () uint8 (0 up, 1 right, 2 down, 3 left), state.agent.pocket (2,) uint8 [tile, colour] ([0, 0] = empty), state.step_num () and state.goal_encoding / state.rule_encoding; action is an int32 in 0..5 (forward, turn right, turn left, pick up, put down, toggle). compute_reward sees the true terminal state of an episode. As in LIMEN, the module may only import jax, jax.numpy (also jax.lax, jax.nn and math); in addition, attribute assignment, private or I/O attributes (load, save, config, debug, callbacks, experimental APIs), frame, code and traceback attributes (gi_frame, f_builtins, f_globals, co_code, tb_frame, ...), attributes named like system modules (os, sys, builtins, importlib, inspect, gc, ...), dunder names other than __name__, class patterns that read such attributes, and exec-like builtins are rejected, and an imported module may only be used as the base of an attribute access (jnp.where), not renamed or passed as a value. Task: pick up the blue pyramid in a 9 x 9 room (XLand-MiniGrid-R1-9x9) that also holds a red ball; the episode ends when the agent picks up the blue pyramid (training episodes last at most 243 steps). Score (maximize): LIMEN's own CascadeEvaluator from Lossfunk/LIMEN@cf0b44da, unchanged, with the task's configuration file: crash filter (syntax, required functions, import, dry run and jit on a real state, observation length <= 512), then PPO from scratch (8,192 parallel environments, 16-step rollouts, one epoch of 16 minibatches, Adam lr 0.001 linearly decayed, gamma 0.99, GAE 0.95, clip 0.2, entropy 0.01, GRU actor-critic with 256-unit observation encoder and 512-unit GRU; LIMEN runs total steps // 131,072 PPO updates) trained on the candidate's observations and rewards. A 500,000-step run (3 updates) with seed 42 must reach 5 % success, otherwise its success rate is the score; candidates that pass are trained with seeds 42, 43 and 44 for 1,000,000 steps (7 updates, 917,504 steps) each and the score is the mean final success rate. Success means the episode ends (goal reached) before the 80-step evaluation horizon; the per-seed rate is measured on 50 evaluation episodes. CPU only, at most four threads; deterministic for a fixed candidate on the same platform and software stack
notes: Evaluator: LIMEN's own CascadeEvaluator (limen/evaluator.py at Lossfunk/LIMEN@cf0b44da, MIT) runs unchanged in a child process with LIMEN's configs/easy_pickup.yaml: crash filter (syntax, required functions, import, dry run and jit on a real state, observation length <= 512), a cascade run of 500,000 steps with seed 42 that must reach 5 % success (otherwise that run's success rate is the score, as LIMEN's archive records it), then PPO with seeds 42, 43 and 44 for 1,000,000 steps each (7 updates of 8,192 environments x 16 steps = 917,504 steps; LIMEN divides without rounding up) and the mean success rate over 50 evaluation episodes per seed with a 80-step horizon. LIMEN's LLM-driven search (prompts, MAP-Elites archive) is not part of the task; one interface is scored per evaluation. The 46 LIMEN files are fetched by scripts/prepare_jax_station.py --limen and checked one by one against catalog/jax_station-data-lock.json. This is LIMEN's in-search fitness (Section 5.3; the 'Cascade' and 'Full' budgets of the paper's Table 3); the paper's main results instead retrain the best interface of each method from scratch with 10 seeds at 2M steps (Section 5.5; Table 3, '10-seed Eval') and report 99 % for joint search on this task, so those values are not comparable with this score.

Additions around the unchanged LIMEN code: the candidate source must pass a static policy before LIMEN sees it (imports limited to jax, jax.numpy, jax.lax, jax.nn and math, where LIMEN's own instructions allow jax and jax.numpy only; no attribute assignment; no private, file I/O, callback, configuration or experimental attributes; no exec-like builtins), and the child process has an audit hook (no subprocesses, sockets or ctypes; writes only in its private temporary directory, where LIMEN writes the candidate file). LIMEN's adapter.run_training is wrapped only to record per-run metrics, and the configuration's relative ruleset path is made absolute. The evaluator reads the candidate's source only (sandboxed.run); no statement of the candidate runs in the evaluator process. The interface is traced inside the child that trains the agent and measures its success, as in LIMEN itself; the static policy and audit hook keep honest interfaces from side effects but are not a proven security boundary.

Hardware and software: CPU instead of the paper's single NVIDIA L4 GPU; jax/jaxlib 0.11.2, flax 0.12.10, optax 0.2.8, distrax 0.1.9 (tfp-nightly 0.26.0.dev20261010), xminigrid 0.9.3 (= dunnolab/xland-minigrid@0d306d14), numpy 2.5.3, Python 3.12; four XLA threads (NPROC/PJRT_NPROC=4) and PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in the child. LIMEN's code runs on these versions without changes.

Seed: LIMEN's default observation (the adapter's flattened grid, position, direction, pocket and step counter) with a sparse reward of 1 on the step that completes the goal, i.e. the paper's Sparse baseline ('raw simulator observations with binary success reward'; the paper's Section 5.1 describes the default observation as a flattened 7 x 7 egocentric grid, XLand-MiniGrid's own view, whereas LIMEN's code uses this full-grid observation in its default and reward-only modes, and its default mode keeps XLand-MiniGrid's built-in reward, 1 - 0.9 x step / max_steps on completion); under random actions in 4,096 environments the reward fired exactly on XLand-MiniGrid's goal events (no misses, no false positives).

Measured (validation/jax_station-checks.json; Apple M4 Max shared with other jobs, load averages 8-37): the seed scores 0.213 (seeds 42/43/44: 0.16, 0.28, 0.20; cascade run 0.14) in 104-220 s wall (322 CPU-seconds, peak memory 2.2 GB), identically in three runs; a constant-zero reward with the same observation scores 0.127 (0.10, 0.14, 0.14); LIMEN's published evolved interface (examples/evolved_interfaces/easy_pickup.py, labelled 'Success rate: 99%') scores 0.993 (1.00, 0.98, 1.00) in 190 s, reproducing the published value. Declared timeout 600 s (child limit 540 s).

Near saturation: strong interfaces reach 0.98-1.00 here, as in the paper (99 % for joint search and 100 % for observation-only search in its 10-seed retraining at 2M steps, Section 5.5; 97-100 % in-search across five search seeds, Appendix B.4), so the task separates weak from strong interfaces but hardly ranks strong ones (resolution 1/150).

Determinism: repeated evaluations of the same candidate in the evaluator's child gave identical per-run success rates, returns and episode lengths (the seed, three times). Results depend on the numerical libraries and their thread settings: with VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS (the thread count of Apple's Accelerate library) unset instead of 4, the same training of LIMEN's published easy interface gave a different final return on its 500,000-step run (6.149 instead of 6.143) and per-seed success rates differing by 0.02 (0.98 instead of 1.00 for seed 42). The evaluator fixes these variables, so scores are reproducible on the same platform and software stack but not across CPU types, BLAS/LAPACK builds or GPUs. valid is null: success rates are sampled estimates after stochastic training; near a success rate of 0.2 the standard error of the 150-episode mean is about 0.035.

Pinned LIMEN evaluator (Lossfunk/LIMEN@cf0b44da, MIT) run unchanged in a child process on CPU JAX (jax 0.11.2, flax 0.12.10, distrax 0.1.9, xminigrid 0.9.3 = dunnolab/xland-minigrid@0d306d14), with LIMEN's configuration, seeds and cascade; the paper used one NVIDIA L4 GPU.

name: Easy pickup
description: Write JAX get_observation(state) and compute_reward(state, action, next_state) for picking up the blue pyramid in a 9 x 9 XLand-MiniGrid room; LIMEN's evaluator trains PPO on them and scores the mean success rate within 80 steps over three 1M-step training seeds, or a 500K-step cascade run's rate if below 5 % (higher is better).
paper_metric: mean success rate across three seeds
